data.exact_reserve_text: The favourable movement in net claims incurred of GBP 12,695 (2014: GBP 8,042,000) primarily derives from benign claims development across most classes of Syndicate 1861's business including Primary Excess of Loss and Single Job Construction.

named_events.loss_description: material exposure to the terrorist attacks in the United States of America on 11 September 2001. The ultimate value of claims arising from this exposure is dependent on the outcome of on-going litigation. Given considerable uncertainty surrounding the eventual outcome of this litigation this translates to uncertainty in the estimated future liabilities.

data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 2255 experienced a net reserve release of GBP 12.695 million in 2015, primarily driven by favourable claims development across most classes of Syndicate 1861's business, including Primary Excess of Loss and Single Job Construction. The syndicate continues to manage its material exposure to the 2001 World Trade Center terrorist attacks, which remains a key area of uncertainty due to ongoing litigation.
raw_causal_phrases: claims improvements on Syndicate 1861, across most classes of business
benign claims development across most classes of Syndicate 1861's business including Primary Excess of Loss and Single Job Construction
data.data_quality_notes: Prior year development figure is reported as 'net claims incurred' movement, not explicitly gross reserve movement. No specific LOB breakdown for prior year development was provided.
